data.name: Gabien
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew root 'gab', meaning 'to be strong'. In the Bible, Gabrielle is the name of an angel who appears to Daniel and announces God's message. This name is a reminder of God's strength and protection.

historical_references.reference: According to early Christian legend, St. Gabien was a bishop in the city of Tours, France, during the 3rd century. He is said to have been a disciple of St. Martin of Tours and was martyred during the Diocletian Persecution in 303 AD.

Another reference to St. Gabien comes from the martyrology of Adomnan, an Irish monk who wrote in the late 7th century. He mentions St. Gabien as a bishop of Tours who was martyred during the reign of Diocletian, though he does not provide a specific year.
